title: Reported speech
subtitle: Reporting what someone else said, with tense and time-word changes

blocks.text: We use reported speech to report what someone else said. When the reporting verb (**said**, etc.) is in the past, we usually move the tense one step back.

rows.example: 'I **want** to build a new house,' said Jill. → Jill said she **wanted** to build a new house.
'We **are making** a dress,' they said. → They said they **were making** a dress.

rows.use: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
rows.example: 'I **have been drawing** all day,' said Debbie. → Debbie said she **had been drawing** all day.
'Jim **made** a card for me yesterday,' Amy said. → Amy said Jim **had made** a card for her the day before.
'I **was writing** a poem,' said Tina. → Tina said she **had been writing** a poem.
'I **will** make you a scarf,' my grandma said. → My grandma said she **would** make me a scarf.

rows.use: am/is/are going to → was/were going to
rows.example: 'They **are going to** make a new one,' said Joe. → Joe said they **were going to** make a new one.
'I **can** draw quite well,' Emma said. → Emma said she **could** draw quite well.
'You **have to** visit the fashion show,' she said. → She said we **had to** visit the fashion show.
'I **may** visit the White House next week,' said Polly. → Polly said she **might** visit the White House the following week.

blocks.intro: We often have to change other words apart from the verb form.
items: pronouns: I → he/she · you → I/me/they/them · we → they · us → them · my → his/her · your → my/their

time and place: here → there · now → then/at that moment · tomorrow → the next day · tonight → that night · next week → the following week · yesterday → the day before · last week → the week before · ago → before

blocks.text: We only make tense changes when the reporting verb (**say**, etc.) is in the past.

blocks.correct: Tony **says** he **is going** to study architecture.
blocks.incorrect: Tony **says** he **was going** to study architecture.

items: We don't change the past perfect simple and the past perfect continuous.
'I **had seen** the picture before.' → He said he **had seen** the picture before.
'I **might** take up painting.' → She said she **might** take up painting.

blocks.intro: We can use verbs like **apologise**, **deny**, **promise**, **refuse** and **suggest** in reported speech.
items: Terence **promised to** help me decorate the house.
Charlotte **refused to** let me see her painting.
My dad **suggested going** to an art gallery.
